division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the south division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's tradesman_dwellings clause. The frame cottages fall on the side streets behind the principal frontages — the back of the same blocks the stores front, which is how a block parcel comes to deal its meanest roof to its worst street. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

married.what_happened: NOT DRAWN FOR THIS HOUSE: MOVED INTO IT. The household model drew this house married and the order book had no woman left in its wife's cell, so no wife was drawn. Margaret Shea headed a house of her own, dealt by T-1174 to fill the women and children the age pyramid lacked; she fits this house by its own rules — her division, a band never above his, no child older than his band allows — and T-2020 folds her house into his: she is his wife here and the 2 of her house come with her. Every name, age band and seed is the one T-1174 drew; the children keep the surname they were dealt with. Both people are the town's invention at the `reconstructed` tier, and the marriage is too: no source says John Baptist married anybody.

kin.note: THE BURIAL ENTRY NAMES THE FATHER, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT IS CLAIMED. Death entry 5 of Father St Cyr's page, Chicago, 2 July 1835: 'On the 2nd of July 1835, I performed the ecclesiastical burial according to the rites of the Catholic Church on the corpse of John Baptist, son of Leon Bourrassa, 28 days old.' Filed as st_cyr_death_05_1 (decedent) and st_cyr_death_05_2 (parent), and both cards were minted from those two rows and carry their record ids, so no identification is being made by name here. THE CHILD WAS ALIVE ON THE SCENE DATE: 28 days old at a burial on 2 July 1835 puts his birth about 4 June 1835 and his death the day AFTER 1 July 1835, so the father and son of this row are father and son in the scene. WHAT THE ENTRY DOES NOT SETTLE: 'John Baptist' is the transcription's reading of the child's name and it is very likely the forename Jean Baptiste standing where a surname was expected — the card is filed under Baptist because that is how the printed register reads, and T-0721 is where names read out of a printer's smudge are ruled on. The RELATIONSHIP does not turn on which of the two the child was called.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('baptist_john:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'John' is read as male because 14 persons in this layer whose sex a source records bear it (bates_john_jr, calhoun_john, caton_john_dean, davis_john, greene_john, hogan_john_s_c, and others), and it stands in the irish and yankee male forename pool of this town's own attested naming. Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.
